newsitem.title: ITALY: Committal hearing for Italy's Prodi adjourned.
newsitem.headline: Committal hearing for Italy's Prodi adjourned.

text.p: A committal hearing that must decide whether Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi should be put on trial for alleged abuse of office was adjourned on Friday until March 19, Prodi's lawyer Paola Severino said.

Severino said examining judge Edoardo Landi had granted a request from another defendant for a court-appointed investigation of the financial transaction at the root of the allegations, linked to Prodi's past chairmanship of state holding IRI.
The allegations relate to IRI's controversial sale of food group Cirio in October 1993 when Prodi was chairman.

Prosecutor Giuseppa Geremia alleges that Prodi and five other IRI board members at the time awarded an "unjust advantage" to a little-known southern Italian consortium, Fis.Vi., in its purchase of Cirio. All deny wrongdoing.
One of the five, Mario Draghi, asked the closed door hearing through his lawyers on Friday to appoint inspectors to examine the transaction.

Landi's decision to allow the inspection means the court will now reconvene on March 19 only to appoint experts to carry it out. They will then have some 60 days to complete their study, delaying proceedings further.
